pr_title: recorder: force dump queued packets when limit reached
pr_body:
```
Some sources can have very long GOPs, going beyond the current queue
limit of 256 packets, leading into recorder (cache-dump) issues when the
recorder insists on dropping frames until it encounters a keyframe,
which is questionable.
We can fix these issues by raising the queue limit even further, but it
may be more apt to just allow av_interleaved_write_frame() do its thing,
and "force" dumping the queue when the limit is reached.
```

or in other words, I'm unsure/lazy about removing the queue itself, or making it only buffer frames at the start.
This works, and fixes #8278 (cache-dumping streams with very long keyframe intervals) without any apparent ill effects.

I'm open to discussion and bikeshedding about the True Solution (remove or adapt the queue? Or am I mistaken and it *is* important?), but the recorder feature is supposed to be experimental and it'd be cooler to have it *work* as soon as possible, and with this patch, it does.
